title: Grade 2 Science — Wed, Jun 25
description: Animals and Their Young Ones — Day 3 of 5: How animals care for young
subject: science

questions.question: How does a mother cat feed her kittens?
options: Feeds them milk from her body
questions.explanation: Mother cats (and all mammals) feed their babies milk produced in their bodies. This is one feature of mammals.

questions.question: A hen sits on her eggs. Why does she do this?
options: To keep the eggs warm so they hatch
To hide the eggs from other animals
questions.explanation: A hen sits on her eggs to keep them warm. The warmth helps the chick develop inside the egg until it is ready to hatch.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of parental care?
options: A dog sleeping in the sun
A mother cow licking her calf
questions.explanation: A mother cow licking her calf is parental care — cleaning and bonding with the young one. The other actions do not involve caring for young ones.

questions.question: How does a father penguin protect the egg in winter?
options: He balances the egg on his feet and covers it with belly fat
He puts it in a tree
questions.explanation: Emperor penguin fathers keep the egg warm by balancing it on their feet and covering it with a warm flap of skin in very cold weather.

questions.question: Which animal does NOT usually care for its young after laying eggs?
questions.explanation: Turtles lay eggs in sand and leave. The eggs hatch on their own and the babies make their way to the sea without parental help.

questions.question: Puppies are born blind and need their mother for food and warmth. This shows that newborn animals:
options: Depend on their parents for survival
questions.explanation: Newborn animals like puppies are helpless at first and depend on their parents for food, warmth and protection. This is why parental care is important.

questions.question: Which action shows a parent PROTECTING its young?
options: A buffalo charging at a lion to save her calf
A crow flying in the sky
A fish swimming in the river
questions.explanation: A buffalo charging at a lion to protect her calf is parental protection. Parents of many species defend their young from predators.

questions.question: A mother bird brings worms to her chicks in the nest. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: When a mother bird brings food to her chicks, she is caring for her young — providing them with nutrition until they can feed themselves.

questions.question: Elephants live in groups called herds. All adult females in the herd help care for the calves. What kind of care is this?
options: Group care by the whole community
questions.explanation: In elephant herds, all adult females (aunts, grandmothers, older sisters) help protect and raise the calves. This is called cooperative or group care.

questions.question: Why do mammals feed their babies milk?
options: Milk is cheap and easy to find
Milk provides the nutrients and energy baby mammals need to grow
All animals feed milk to their young
questions.explanation: Milk contains proteins, fats and other nutrients perfectly suited to the baby mammal's needs. It provides energy and helps the baby grow and develop immunity.

questions.question: A mother cat teaches her kittens to hunt. Why is this important?
options: So the kittens can survive on their own when they grow up
Because the mother cat is tired of hunting
So they can teach other cats
questions.explanation: Teaching young animals to hunt (or find food) is essential for survival. Once the kittens grow up, they must be able to feed themselves.

questions.question: Compare: A hen sits on eggs for 21 days. A dog's puppies can hear after 2–3 weeks. Which shows longer parental investment before young are independent?
options: Hen, because 21 days of incubation comes first
Dog, because puppies need many months of care
Both need exactly the same time
questions.explanation: While a hen incubates eggs for 21 days, chicks become independent quickly. Dog puppies need weeks of feeding, warmth and teaching — making the dog's overall parental investment longer.

questions.question: Why do animals that lay many eggs (like fish) often provide LESS care per egg compared to animals like elephants?
options: Laying many eggs means more will survive even without care; elephants have few young so each calf receives more attention
Fish do not have young ones
questions.explanation: Fish may lay thousands of eggs; even if most are eaten, some survive. Elephants have very few calves (one at a time), so each calf is precious and receives years of intensive care.

questions.question: A baby deer can walk within hours of birth. A human baby cannot walk for about a year. What does this tell us?
options: Deer are more intelligent than humans
Different animals develop at different rates; deer need to escape predators quickly
Deer do not need parental care
questions.explanation: Deer live in open areas with predators, so they must be mobile quickly. Human babies take longer to develop but their brains grow in complexity over years.

questions.question: Parental care in animals is most important for which reason?
options: To help young ones survive until they can take care of themselves
To teach young animals to fight each other
questions.explanation: Parental care ensures that young animals — which are often vulnerable and helpless at birth — survive, grow and develop the skills needed for independence.
